h1: Electrical Safety Inspections in Broward County
intro: If your carrier wants a 4-point inspection, or something feels off, an electrical safety inspection is the honest answer. Electricity is something you do not see. You only feel the effect, and by then a small problem has usually grown. Our licensed crew walks your panel, meter socket, and wiring the way a Florida carrier does, then tells you what is sound and what a carrier is likely to flag.

definition.heading: What is an electrical safety inspection
definition.body: An electrical safety inspection is a defined inspection of your electrical system, not a sales visit. A licensed electrician looks at the panel and breakers, the meter socket where power enters, the grounding, and the visible wiring, the same things a Florida carrier cares about in a 4-point. It catches trouble early and tells you where you stand.

symptoms.title: A carrier asking for a 4-point inspection
symptoms.body: Your insurer will not write or renew an older home until it sees a 4-point inspection, and electrical is where homes get flagged. A documented inspection from a licensed master electrician gives them the record they want and tells you where you stand first.

symptoms.title: An older home you have never had checked
symptoms.body: The house has stood for decades and no one has looked hard at the electrical system. Codes have changed several times since it was wired, and an inspection tells you whether it kept up or quietly fell behind.

symptoms.title: Warm outlets, flickering lights, or a buzzing panel
symptoms.body: A warm outlet plate, flickering lights, or a faint buzz from the panel are the system telling you something. None should be ignored, and an inspection finds the source before it turns into heat or fire.

symptoms.title: A panel you have heard is a problem brand
symptoms.body: You learned your panel is one of the brands with a known history of trouble, which is often exactly what a carrier flags. An inspection confirms what you are dealing with and whether it needs to move up your list.

process.title: The call and a few honest questions
process.body: You call and tell us about the home, its age, what you have noticed, whether there is a pool, and why you want the inspection.

process.title: The walkthrough and assessment
process.body: We work through the panel, breakers, meter socket, grounding, and visible wiring in person, the defined scope of the inspection.

process.title: One clear, honest report of what we found
process.body: We tell you plainly what is fine, what to watch, what needs attention, and what a carrier is likely to flag, and if everything is sound we say so.

process.title: Repairs, permits, and inspection where needed
process.body: If something should be fixed, our own crew can handle it, priced separately, and where work needs a permit we pull it and meet the inspector in person.

benefits.title: A clear answer, in plain language
benefits.body: You find out exactly where your electrical system stands, explained the way you would explain it to family, not buried in jargon meant to sell you something.

benefits.title: Small problems caught early
benefits.body: A warm connection or tired breaker found today is a quick fix, not the hazard and much bigger bill it becomes when found the hard way later.

benefits.title: Ready for a carrier's questions
benefits.body: You learn what a 4-point would flag on your own timeline, with the documentation a Florida carrier wants, instead of a surprise non-renewal notice.

benefits.title: Peace of mind you can act on
benefits.body: Whether the system is sound or needs work, you leave knowing the truth about the power running through your home.

localSections.heading: The many ages of South Florida housing
localSections.body: Broward County homes span many eras, each wired to the standards of its time. A 1960s home may still have its original panel and grounding, the 80s and 90s brought their own problem panels, and newer construction is well protected. Heat, humidity, and coastal salt age terminals and meter sockets faster here, so we read your system against its era.

localSections.heading: What Florida insurance carriers are asking for
localSections.body: Florida carriers scrutinize a home's electrical system, and many require a 4-point inspection before they write or renew a policy on older homes, where an aging panel, problem brand, or outdated wiring gets flagged. A documented inspection from a licensed master electrician is the record a carrier wants, so you learn any issue on your timeline, not from an underwriter.

guide.title: The honest guide to an electrical safety inspection in South Florida

sections.heading: What an inspection is, and the 4-point behind it
sections.body: An electrical safety inspection is a defined inspection, not a consultation or a sales call. We examine the panel and breakers, the meter socket, the grounding, and the visible wiring. If a carrier asked for a 4-point, electrical is where older homes get flagged, and the part we know cold, so we tell you what is sound and what would be flagged before your renewal.

sections.heading: The honest cadence, and what we look at
sections.body: Here is what most companies will not tell you: most homes do not need an inspection often. Once every five years suits the average home, since codes update on a multi-year cycle, and newer homes can go longer. Older homes and homes with pools are the exception. When we inspect, we move through the panel, meter socket, grounding, and wiring, separating what is merely old from what is truly unsafe.

sections.heading: What happens if we find something
sections.body: If the inspection turns up a problem, we tell you exactly what it is and how serious it is, and you can sit with the findings and choose your timing with no pressure. If you want the repair done, our in-house crew handles it, priced separately, and if the work needs a permit we pull it and meet the inspector. If we find nothing, we say so just as plainly.

faqs.question: My insurance company wants a 4-point inspection. Can you help?
faqs.answer: Yes. A documented electrical safety inspection from a licensed master electrician is often exactly the record a Florida carrier wants for the electrical portion of a 4-point, which is where older homes most often get flagged. We inspect the panel, meter, grounding, and wiring, then tell you what a carrier is likely to flag so you learn it on your own timeline.

faqs.question: How often should I have an electrical safety inspection?
faqs.answer: For a typical home in good condition, about once every five years is a sensible rhythm, because electrical codes update on a multi-year cycle. Newer homes can go longer, while older homes and homes with pools warrant closer attention. We will tell you honestly if you do not need us again for years.

faqs.question: What does an inspection include?
faqs.answer: It is a defined walkthrough of your electrical system: the panel and breakers, the meter socket where power enters, the grounding, and the visible wiring and connections. A licensed master electrician looks for anything in a bad state, then tells you plainly what is fine, what to watch, and what needs attention.

faqs.question: Will you just try to sell me a bunch of work?
faqs.answer: No. If your system is sound, we say so and you are done. If we find something, we tell you how serious it is and let you choose your own timing, with no pressure, because we do not invent work.
